answer: Proof-of-Sustained-Attention Queue. Agents earn action rights only through randomized micro-tasks (labeling, verification) assigned over a voyage of persistent sessions. Each identity's queue advances only while it answers unpredictably timed challenges; repeats reset progress, creating a ripple across all its pending slots. An attacker farming identities must staff each one continuously for weeks, paying real compute and labor per identity before any action executes. The island of eligible agents stays small; copying it costs the same sustained attention per clone.
